Conditional Z-Estimation with DNN weights

Source: vignettes/conditional-z-estimation.Rmd
conditional-z-estimation.Rmd

Overview

This vignette shows how DNN localization can be used in three user-level estimators:

  • np_dnn() for localized conditional means
  • cate_dnn() for conditional average treatment effects
  • plqr_dnn() for localized PLQR coefficient surfaces and orthogonal moments

Each wrapper supports:

  • matrix and data-frame interfaces
  • DNN method choice ("exact" or "asymp")
  • delete-1 jackknife SEs ("fast", "loo", "none")
  • modular kernel-order tuning via tuning = tuning_dnn_paper(...)
  • fitted-object diagnostics via diagnostics()

The wrappers implement fixed top-k DNN kernels for 1 <= k <= s. Extending the written 1-NN theory to fixed k is essentially direct, but the current accompanying manuscript derivations are stated for k = 1.

Local Mean (np_dnn) 

demo_np <- np_demo_data(n = 250, p = 2, design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1)

fit_np <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_default,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = "fast",
  return = c("W", "ess", "tuning")
)

fit_np$mu
fit_np$se
diagnostics(fit_np)

CATE (cate_dnn)

cate_dnn() supports either:

  • Full AIPW nuisance inputs (m0, m1, e)
  • Robinson-form nuisance inputs (m, e)
  • Direct pseudo_outcome 
demo_cate <- cate_demo_data(n = 300, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 1)
df <- demo_cate$data
df$m1_oracle <- df$m0_oracle + df$tau_oracle

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = df,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  t_col = "D",
  m0_col = "m0_oracle",
  m1_col = "m1_oracle",
  e_col = "e_oracle",
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_default,
  se = TRUE,
  return = c("W", "psi", "nuisance", "tuning")
)

summary(fit_cate)
confint(fit_cate)
diagnostics(fit_cate)
predict(fit_cate, x0 = c(0.2, -0.1), interval = "confidence")

PLQR Orthogonal Moments and Coefficient Inference (plqr_dnn) 

demo_plqr <- plqr_demo_data(n = 250, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 1)
# demo_plqr$data$density_oracle holds the true threshold density of the
# demo DGP (constant, 4 * tau * (1 - tau) / sigma).

fit_plqr <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo_plqr$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle",
  theta_eval = demo_plqr$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_default,
  se = TRUE,
  return = c("W", "score", "ess", "tuning")
)

summary(fit_plqr)
confint(fit_plqr)
predict(fit_plqr, x0 = c(0.25, -0.25), interval = "confidence")
fit_plqr$moment
diagnostics(fit_plqr)

PLQR nuisances and inference

plqr_dnn() localizes the moment

𝔼[(τ−𝟏{Y≤D⊤θ+g0(U)})(D−mD(U))|X≈x0] \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\tau - \mathbf{1}\{Y \le D^\top \theta + g_0(U)\}\right) \left(D - m_D(U)\right) \;\middle|\; X \approx x_0 \right]

at the supplied coefficient value theta_eval. Here g is the partially-linear model’s nonparametric shape nuisance (paper notation g0(U)g_0(U)), not itself a quantile — the sum D′θ0+g0D'\theta_0 + g_0 is the conditional quantile. mD residualizes the design (m0(U)=E[D∣U]m_0(U) = E[D \mid U]). Both are supplied by the user; no nuisance model is fit internally, and no root solving is performed: the result’s theta repeats the supplied theta_eval (meta$theta_source = "supplied").

Coefficient-level standard errors and confidence intervals require supplying density/density_col (an estimate of the local conditional density of Y at the fitted quantile). This is not an optional convenience: every valid coefficient route needs the density-backed sandwich bread (see markdown_notes/design/15_plqr_variance_estimation_rationale.md). Two coefficient-meat routes are available through theta_meat: the analytic score covariance (default) and a full delete-1 jackknife covariance of the localized vector moment (theta_meat = "jackknife", stored in moment_vcov). A fit without a density input can still report moment_se (a componentwise jackknife SE on the moment, useful as a diagnostic) but confint()/predict(se.fit = TRUE) will error, by design, until refit with a density input — a componentwise moment_se alone is never coefficient inference. Coefficient-level results live in theta_se / theta_vcov; the routes are never mixed in one field.

Diagnostics and Reporting

The three wrappers return enough retained state for diagnostics() to compute fit-level summaries without rerunning the estimator.

d_np <- diagnostics(fit_np)
d_cate <- diagnostics(fit_cate)
d_plqr <- diagnostics(fit_plqr)

d_np[, c("target_id", "n_eff", "weighted_mean_y")]
d_cate[, c("target_id", "treated_mass", "control_mass", "treated_share")]
d_plqr[, c("target_id", "gram_min_eig", "gram_condition_number")]

General diagnostics summarize weight concentration, realized distance radii when dx was retained, and tuning metadata. Estimator-specific diagnostics add NP outcome summaries, CATE overlap summaries, and PLQR residual-regressor Gram conditioning.

Notes on Standard Errors

np_dnn() and cate_dnn() always use delete-1 jackknife SEs when se = TRUE.

  • "fast" reuses full-sample ranks and applies rank updates per deletion.
  • "loo" recomputes leave-one-out weights directly (reference-equivalent).
  • "none" skips SE computation.

s < n is required when jackknife SEs are requested.

plqr_dnn() differs: when density/density_col is supplied, se = TRUE reports the direct coefficient sandwich instead of a jackknife SE (the jackknife path is not used in that case); the moment-level jackknife SE described above is only used as a fallback diagnostic when no density input is supplied. See “PLQR nuisances and inference” above.
